name: frozen-sampled-rollout-protocol-v0.1

protocol.selection: For each feasible next action, estimate immediate measured cost plus base-policy cost-to-go by Monte Carlo sampling from a deliberately miscalibrated branch-probability model; choose the minimum estimated action, execute one action under the true environment distribution, observe, and replan.
protocol.branch_miscalibration: Multiply each true branch probability by independent mean-preserving log-normal noise at each state/action and normalize before Monte Carlo sampling.
protocol.actual_evaluation: Expected cost is always accumulated under the true branch distribution and compared to exact unrestricted dynamic-programming optimal cost.

guardrail: No third-sealed-test world seed, result, or post-hoc tuning may be added to this artifact. Sample counts, branch-noise levels, and base-policy noise are frozen here before the next test worlds are introduced.
claim_boundary: Synthetic controller robustness protocol. Sampling from a perturbed finite-world transition model is a stress proxy for imperfect predictive value estimation, not an empirical LLM world-model calibration distribution.
